realtimeReason.route: the real time endpoint is missing on the server

dashboard.title: Monitors
dashboard.subtitle: {up} up · {down} down · {paused} paused
dashboard.emptyHint: Create your first monitor to start collecting heartbeats.
dashboard.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, description or tag
dashboard.degradedWarning: One or more cluster nodes are unavailable; the votes of the missing nodes are excluded.

monitor.retriesHelp: How many extra attempts before the monitor is considered down.
monitor.resendHelp: 0 notifies only when the status changes. A positive value repeats the alert while the monitor stays down.
monitor.timeoutHelp: Maximum duration of a single check.
monitor.upsideDownHelp: The monitor is up when the target is unreachable (for example a firewall rule that must keep blocking).
monitor.runOnHelp: Which cluster nodes execute this check. Every node votes and the failure strategy decides the final status.
monitor.cacheBusterHelp: Appends a randomly generated uptime_kuma_cachebuster query parameter to every request, so caches and CDNs answer fresh.
monitor.acceptedCodesHelp: Ranges and codes separated by commas, for example 200-299,301.
monitor.keywordPlaceholder: Text that must appear in the response
monitor.tcpHelp: The monitor connects, optionally sends the payload and validates the answer.
monitor.dnsInvertHelp: With an expected value: up when the value is absent. Without a value: up when the name does not resolve.
monitor.deleteWarning: The monitor and all of its heartbeats will be removed. This cannot be undone.
monitor.pauseWarning: Pausing stops the checks until you resume the monitor.
monitor.sslServerNameHelp: Optional: the name sent during the handshake (needed when the certificate depends on the virtual host).
monitor.sslHelp: A ssl monitor checks the handshake; with “ignore TLS errors” it also reports a self signed certificate as up.
monitor.certHelp: Watch the TLS certificate of this target: the days left are shown here and the reminders reach the channels.
monitor.certNotify: Notify when it is about to expire
monitor.certWarnDaysHelp: Free list, e.g. 7,6,5,30. Each value alerts once when it is crossed; below the smallest one the reminder repeats once a day.
monitor.domainHelp: Watch the registry expiration of this target's domain: RDAP is tried first, then a per-TLD WHOIS parser (Admin > TLD/SSL expiration). Add a manual date for TLDs that publish none.
monitor.domainNotify: Notify when it is about to expire
monitor.domainWarnDaysHelp: Free list, e.g. 7,6,5,30. Same cadence as the certificate: each value alerts once when it is crossed; below the smallest one the reminder repeats once a day.
monitor.domainExpiresAtHelp: Optional. When set it replaces the RDAP/WHOIS lookup, which is how a TLD that publishes no date is still watched.
monitor.templateHelp: Follow a template: editing the template pushes its defaults to every monitor linked to it. The groups and the tags are never touched.
monitor.groupsHelp: Groups organise the monitor list and feed the status pages that include them.
monitor.cloneHelp: The copy starts with a clean history: the heartbeats are not copied.
monitor.runOnSomeHelp: Comma separated node ids. Only these nodes probe the monitor, and only they vote on its status.

groups.title: Monitor groups
groups.subtitle: Named collections of monitors: a status page that includes a group shows every monitor inside it
groups.name: Group name
groups.monitorsHelp: Select the monitors that belong to this group.
groups.noMonitors: No monitor in this group yet
groups.emptyHint: Create a group to organise the monitors and publish them together on a status page.
groups.cloneDeep: Clone the monitors of the group
groups.cloneDeepHelp: Every monitor is duplicated with a (copy) suffix; the heartbeat history is not copied.
groups.copyLinks: Copy the channels and the groups of each monitor
groups.deleteWarning: The group is removed; the monitors inside it stay untouched.

templates.title: Monitor templates
templates.subtitle: Reusable blueprints: a probe configuration plus the defaults applied in bulk
templates.emptyHint: Create a template to add monitors in bulk or to apply the same configuration to many monitors at once.
templates.channels: Notification channels applied to the monitors
templates.deleteWarning: The template is removed; the monitors created from it stay untouched.
templates.certHelp: Certificate watching applied to the monitors created from this template.
templates.domainHelp: Domain expiration watching applied to the monitors created from this template.
templates.propagate: Update the linked monitors when this template changes
templates.propagateHelp: Every monitor that follows this template receives the defaults above when it is edited (never the groups or the tags).
templates.linkAll: Link every monitor of this type
templates.linkAllTitle: Link the monitors to this template
templates.linkAllWarning: Every monitor of this type starts following the template and receives its defaults. Groups and tags are left untouched.
templates.linkAllPreview: {monitors} monitors of this type: {linked} will follow the template and {updated} keep a different value.

expiry.title: TLD/SSL expiration
expiry.subtitle: Daily certificate and domain checks, one lookup per unique target, plus the WHOIS rules for the TLDs without RDAP
expiry.cadenceHelp: Certificates and domains are checked once a day and deduplicated: several monitors on the same host or domain share a single lookup.
expiry.settingsHelp: When and how fast the daily checks run
expiry.checkTimeHelp: The local time (in the timezone below) when the daily check runs.
expiry.timezoneHelp: IANA name, e.g. UTC or America/Sao_Paulo.
expiry.rateLimitHelp: Minimum delay between two registry lookups. 0 disables it; the default is 100 ms (10 lookups/s).
expiry.timeoutHelp: How long a single RDAP or WHOIS lookup may take.
expiry.parsersHelp: Rules that read the expiration date of a raw WHOIS response. They are the only option for TLDs without RDAP and for the ones that do not publish a machine readable date.
expiry.noParsersHelp: A monitor on a TLD without RDAP reports "unsupported" until a rule exists here or a manual date is set in the monitor.
expiry.targetsHelp: What the job actually looks up: monitors that share an endpoint or a registrable domain are a single row.
expiry.noTargetsHelp: Turn on "Watch certificate" or "Watch domain" in a monitor and it appears here after the next run.
expiry.tldHelp: The suffix without a dot, e.g. br or com.br. The most specific rule wins.
expiry.serverHelp: Optional. When empty the registry server is discovered through whois.iana.org.
expiry.regexHelp: RE2 expression whose first capture group holds the date, e.g. expires at:\s*(.+)
expiry.layoutsHelp: Go reference layouts separated by ';', e.g. 2006-01-02. Common layouts are tried automatically.
expiry.notFoundHelp: Optional regex that marks the domain as free, e.g. (?i)no match for
expiry.rateOverrideHelp: Optional per-registry delay; the larger of this and the global rate limit wins. 0 = use the global one.
expiry.testHelp: Run the rule against a live domain, or paste a raw WHOIS response.
expiry.testRawHelp: When filled, the rule is applied to this text instead of querying the registry.
expiry.testNotFound: The rule reports the domain as not registered
expiry.deleteParserWarning: Monitors on this TLD fall back to a manual date (or report unsupported) until another rule matches.

bulk.title: Add monitors in bulk
bulk.help: Paste one monitor per line. The template decides how they are probed.
bulk.formatHelp: Columns: name,target[,type,keyword,tags,interval]. A header row like name,url is ignored, # starts a comment and comma, semicolon or tab all work.
bulk.groups: Add them to these groups too

apply.title: Apply a template to monitors
apply.help: Overwrite the selected fields of many monitors at once.
apply.fieldsHelp: Only the checked fields are overwritten.
apply.configNotice: The probe options are applied without the target: every monitor keeps its own URL, host or hostname.
apply.monitorsHelp: Select the monitors that receive the template.

notifications.title: Notification channels
notifications.subtitle: Alerts delivered when a monitor changes status
notifications.emptyHint: Create an SMTP or Webhook channel to receive alerts.
notifications.webhookBodyHelp: Go template with the alert variables, for example {'{{'}.Event{'}}'} or {'{{'}.MonitorName{'}}'}. Leave it empty to use the default JSON body.
notifications.webhookHeadersHelp: Sent with every request: use it for an Authorization token or a signature header.
notifications.linkedMonitorsHelp: Without any link the channel receives no alerts.
notifications.deleteWarning: The channel will be removed from every monitor.

statusPages.title: Status pages
statusPages.subtitle: Public read-only pages you can share with your users
statusPages.emptyHint: Create a public page and pick the monitors to display.
statusPages.isPublicHelp: Disabled: only authenticated administrators can preview the page.
statusPages.selectMonitorsHelp: The list order defines the display order.
statusPages.selectGroupsHelp: Every monitor of the group is shown, so adding a monitor to the group publishes it here.
statusPages.badgeHelp: SVG badge ready to be embedded in a README.
statusPages.deleteWarning: The public page stops responding immediately.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Public API tokens and the IP allow/deny list
security.tokensHelp: Used in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header of /api/v1.
security.tokenCreated: Copy the token now: it will not be shown again.
security.ipRulesHelp: With no rule everything is allowed. As soon as an allow rule exists the scope becomes an allow list.
security.bypassWarning: IP rules are disabled because SECURITY_BYPASS_IP_RULES=true.
security.lockoutWarning: Careful: denying your own address on the Everything scope locks you out of the dashboard. Use the database or SECURITY_BYPASS_IP_RULES to recover.

cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.subtitle: Several dashboards synchronised as one cluster
cluster.disabledHint: Set CLUSTER_ENABLED=true on this node to join a cluster.
cluster.privateKeyHelp: Share this key with the other nodes when they join. It lives in the shared settings table.
cluster.regenerateWarning: Every node must join again with the new key.
cluster.joinHelp: Provide the primary node URL and the cluster private key.
cluster.failureAnyHelp: The monitor goes down as soon as one node reports a failure.
cluster.failureAllHelp: The monitor goes down only when every online node fails.
cluster.failureQuorumHelp: The monitor goes down when the majority fails; a partial failure shows as degraded.
cluster.nodeUnavailableHelp: Nodes without a heartbeat for more than 2 minutes stop voting. With MARK_DEGRADED their absence is surfaced as a warning.
cluster.notificationSenderHelp: ANY_WITH_LOCK uses a database lock to avoid duplicated notifications.
cluster.syncUnavailable: Synchronisation is not enabled on this node.
cluster.quorumHint: With the QUORUM strategy the denominator is the nodes this node can reach, so a partitioned minority can decide with fewer nodes than the cluster has. Check that every node is reachable.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Locale and theme defaults for new visitors
settings.timeFormatHelp: How times are displayed. Automatic follows the browser; the other two force a 12 or 24 hour clock.
settings.defaultsHelp: Applied only to visitors who have not chosen a language or theme in their browser yet.

about.title: About
about.description: Up is a minimalist uptime monitor written in Go and Vue, ready to run as a cluster on top of an external database.
